newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia allocates 400,000 bbls more LSWR in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allocates 400,000 bbls more LSWR in Oct.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company, Pertamina has allocated an additional 400,000 barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for loading in October, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Sources said two Pertamina affiliates, Pacific Petroleum and Indoil has each been allocated 200,000 barrels.
But details on loading schedules were not immediately available.

The additional allocation was a result of surplus LSWR which were stored in tanks following a delay in starting up a 55,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) visbreaker at Indonesia's Cilacap refinery earlier in October.
The visbreaker start-up problems had occured following a maintenance shutdown of a 200,000-bpd crude distillation unit.
While the CDU resumed normal operations on October 7, the visbreaker was ony able to restart on October 13.
Pertamina had earlier allocated a total of 3.8 million barrels of LSWR for October loading.
LSWR is fed into a visbreaker to reduce its viscosity, or to lighten its waxy texture, and to produce naphtha and distillates.
